codes: IEEE 1547-2018, FERC SGIP Supplemental Review (100% of Minimum Load Screen), ANSI C84.1

hard_constraints.parameter: ANSI C84.1 Range A Steady-State Voltage
Short-Circuit Duty Margin on Feeder Breakers

pe_disposition:
The supplemental review for the proposed 4.5 MW AC PV+BESS interconnection was performed strictly under IEEE 1547-2018 (voltage regulation, ride-through, and interoperability), FERC SGIP Supplemental Review (100 % of minimum daytime load penetration screen), and ANSI C84.1 Range A. Governing relations comprise the three-phase Newton–Raphson power-flow solution of the network admittance matrix, the linearized voltage-change expression \(\Delta V/V \approx (\Delta P\cdot R+\Delta Q\cdot X)/|V|^2\) for rapid voltage change (RVC), and the IEC 61000-4-15 / IEEE 1453 short- and long-term flicker perceptibility indices \(P_{st}\) and \(P_{lt}\) obtained from time-series voltage traces. Boundary conditions include feeder minimum daytime load (generation not to exceed 100 % of that load), fixed substation LTC tap, zero reverse power at the substation transformer, and DER inverter current-injection limits. The physical methodology consisted of unbalanced three-phase load-flow and short-circuit studies with the PV+BESS modeled as a voltage-source inverter capable of four-quadrant operation, evaluated under coincident minimum-load / maximum-generation and maximum-load / minimum-generation cases, including BESS charge/discharge cycling.

All four hard constraints are satisfied with a global compliance index G = 1. Steady-state voltages remain inside ANSI C84.1 Range A (computed 0.984–1.031 pu versus required 0.950–1.050 pu). Primary-feeder RVC is 1.78 % (limit 3.00 %). Substation reverse power is identically 0.00 MW, confirming the 100 % minimum-load screen. Feeder-breaker short-circuit duty is 74.6 % of interrupting rating (limit 90 %). Flicker and grounding/protection screens likewise remain within IEEE 1547 and utility interconnection criteria; therefore the project passes Supplemental Review without requiring a full Facilities Study.

I, a Licensed Professional Engineer, hereby sign off the study as complete, accurate, and code-compliant. Quality-assurance checks comprised independent model validation against as-built feeder data, sensitivity runs on load and irradiance, and peer review of relay-coordination settings. Residual risk is mitigated by requiring IEEE 1547-2018 certified inverters with voltage/frequency ride-through, real-time telemetry of reverse-power and voltage, and a post-commissioning measurement campaign to confirm \(P_{st}/P_{lt}\) and RVC remain within the computed margins. The interconnection may proceed to construction subject to the stated operating limits.
